timeWindow.title: The same cost-first policy in ample and urgent campaign contexts
timeWindow.sharedBasis: 120 usable kits by minute 1,440; a $600 limit; faults in both the printed code and destination. The same frozen cost-first apps in calculation workflow 4.0.0 prefers lower expense among complete corrections that meet every requirement. Both scenarios plan ten minutes of fresh rehearsal.
timeWindow.change: Compare two campaigns with their own scoped diagnostic and booking records. Review begins at minute 0 in one and 1,410 in the other. Candidate starts follow that clock; the cutoff, quotes, capacity and recorded validity intervals stay fixed.

panels.label: Ample window · GIFT-320
panels.explanation: Leah can put forward the cheaper complete correction. Both packages meet the deadline, so finance has no deadline-based reason to pay the extra $100.

figure.alt: The SDK Decision summary prefers complete in-house correction at $300; the $400 external package also meets the one-day cutoff.
figure.caption: With the full day available, the cost-first profile supports the $300 complete correction.

panels.label: Thirty minutes remain · GIFT-321
panels.explanation: Leah can justify the $100 premium because the cheaper complete response misses the original cutoff. The external package still needs a genuine current booking.

figure.alt: With thirty minutes remaining, the $400 external complete correction finishes at minute 1,435; the cheaper complete correction is too late.
figure.caption: The premium is justified by the actual cutoff. The fixed priority still prefers lower complete expense among eligible arrangements.

timeWindow.takeaway: The priority stays cost first. The available time determines whether the $300 package meets the promise and whether paying $400 protects it. Choosing and authorizing that work remain separate human actions.

booking.title: The same urgent campaign with a current or old-scope external booking
booking.sharedBasis: The same GIFT-321 case: 120 kits by minute 1,440, review at 1,410, a $600 limit, the same faults, quotes, starts, resources, permissions and v3 cost-first app. External complete correction costs $400 and would finish at 1,435.
booking.change: Exactly one applied input changes: the insert revision stated by the external booking. The current campaign configuration, quotes, permissions, resources and timing stay fixed.

panels.label: Booking covers the current insert
panels.explanation: Leah can propose external work on this recorded basis, then obtain authorization and coordinate execution. The quote and correctly scoped booking support different parts of that proposal.

figure.alt: The same GIFT-321 campaign has a current insert-4 external booking and supports the $400 complete correction.
figure.caption: This paired calculation retains every other applied business input.

panels.label: Booking covers the previous insert

inputs.label: Remaining alternative
inputs.value: In-house work finishes at 1,450: too late

panels.explanation: Leah needs a genuine booking for the current configuration or an escalation. Rewriting the old confirmation to match the new insert would manufacture support.

figure.alt: Changing only the external booking’s insert revision from insert-4 to insert-3 leaves no passing complete correction for GIFT-321.
figure.caption: The campaign configuration remains insert-4. Its booking must cover the actual work.

booking.takeaway: The price and promised speed are unchanged. A source record that covers the actual work determines whether that response is available; a meaningful result can be “obtain support or escalate.”

authorRehearsal.title: Five- and ten-minute case inputs under the same adapted ten-minute minimum
authorRehearsal.sharedBasis: The same separately adapted app and workflow require at least ten minutes of fresh rehearsal. The original 120-kit, minute-1,440 promise, $600 limit, observations, quotes and missing external confirmation remain fixed. This authoring release is separate from the v3 operating profile.
authorRehearsal.change: Only the planned fresh-rehearsal answer changes: five minutes versus ten. Both views already use the stronger mandatory minimum.

panels.label: Five minutes supplied
panels.finding: No complete correction meets the new rule.

inputs.label: Business response
inputs.value: Revise the proposal; the shortfall stays visible

panels.explanation: Leah cannot put forward this case as satisfying production’s new policy. Publishing a stronger requirement must not silently change her answer.

figure.alt: The separately adapted ten-minute-minimum app rejects complete correction plans while the case still supplies five minutes.
figure.caption: The stronger rule does not edit Leah’s answer. The focused finding shows that no complete option meets the commitment.

navigationFigure.alt: The separate adapted ten-minute-minimum release blocks complete corrections while the case supplies five minutes.
navigationFigure.caption: The stronger requirement leaves the original five-minute case input untouched. No complete correction passes.

panels.label: Ten minutes supplied
panels.explanation: Leah can put forward the complete in-house sequence under the new rule. Finance sees the same $300 expense; marketing sees that the longer planned check still fits the one-day window.

figure.alt: The same adapted ten-minute-minimum app supports $300 internal correction with a ten-minute rehearsal and handoff at minute 40.
figure.caption: Ten minutes supplied under the same ten-minute requirement restores the complete internal correction. Choosing and authorizing remain separate.

navigationFigure.alt: The same adapted release supports the $300 internal correction with ten minutes planned and handoff at minute 40.
navigationFigure.caption: The case now supplies ten minutes under the same stronger requirement. People still authorize and carry out the work.

authorRehearsal.takeaway: The author changes a reusable requirement in a deliberate new release. Leah supplies a case that meets it. The review exposes the consequence of each input; an actual passed rehearsal still needs its own operating record.

calculationBudget.title: The same complete corrections under two spending boundaries
calculationBudget.sharedBasis: Current Plan a gift-kit commitment workflow 2.1.0, 120 kits by minute 1,440, the same scoped observations, quotes, resources, permissions and current external booking. Both cases plan ten minutes of fresh rehearsal under the unchanged five-minute minimum.
calculationBudget.change: Only the applied expense limit changes: $600 versus $200. Recalculate retains the unchanged evidence calculation and reassesses planning against the new boundary.

panels.label: $600 available

inputs.label: Calculated basis
inputs.value: Both established faults must be corrected

panels.explanation: Leah can propose the cheaper complete response. Both packages meet the original deadline and recorded requirements.

figure.alt: The current planning calculation prefers internal replacement and journey repair at $300, with complete external correction available at $400.
figure.caption: Both complete corrections pass under the confirmed one-day case. The cost-first workflow prefers $300 internal work; the case plans ten minutes under a five-minute minimum.

panels.label: $200 available

inputs.label: Calculated basis
inputs.value: The same established faults and fixed rules

panels.explanation: Leah needs another supported package, an appropriate change of spending authority or an escalation. Recalculation cannot turn a partial repair into a complete one.

figure.alt: Recalculation under the $200 limit finds no complete correction meeting the recorded requirements.
figure.caption: The $100 and $180 partial fixes remain insufficient; the $300 and $400 complete packages exceed the changed boundary. A complete calculation can establish that no supplied option fits.

calculationBudget.takeaway: A complete calculation can establish that no supplied arrangement fits. The changed spending boundary withdraws the earlier proposal without erasing its original calculation.
